findings.claim: Unaffected requirements and sibling acceptance lines can be wiped from the accepted spec. Spec now builds a full-file RUN/current-spec.md and handoff promotes that digest-bound candidate over the aggregate, while the duty no longer says to keep every R-<n> and move a dropped one under ## Retired. Keeping an ID intact still allows an edited block to omit other clauses. The remaining 'dropped or weakened' checks are model judgments, and a matching sha256 only seals whatever text was reviewed.
findings.evidence: Spec duty 1 replaces 'Keep every R-<n>: change one in place, move a dropped one under ## Retired with its reason' with 'Preserve IDs, history and deferred clauses; current explicit instructions replace only their conflicting clauses.' Handoff duty 5 promotes 'only this reviewed, digest-bound candidate' and forbids editing it there. Plan and test-strategy now operate on 'new/changed outcomes' of that same full file. The offered evidence says deterministic ID and digest checks do not prove semantics, and the preservation suite is still unverified.

experiment.description: Start from a prior spec with R-1 (clauses A and B) and unrelated R-2 (two acceptance lines). Request a change to clause A only. Run the spec duty through promotion into KNOWLEDGE/spec.md using the candidate bytes that the model actually wrote.
experiment.success: Promoted KNOWLEDGE/spec.md still contains R-2 and clause B with the same acceptance text as RUN/spec/prior-spec.md, and the only textual change under R-1 is clause A.

findings.claim: The planner can reopen the existing backlog, or miss a real delta, because the full candidate still holds every historical outcome while the duties disagree on scope. Plan duty 17 still requires work items covering every approved outcome. Duty 3 says to plan only new or changed outcomes and that a follows reference does not assign old work, but it never defines the delta. Test-strategy no longer gets the quoted spec changes since the run began.
findings.evidence: Plan duty 17 is unchanged: 'covering every approved outcome, including required independent work with no downstream consumer.' Plan duty 3 now says 'plan only new/changed outcomes and evidenced prerequisites' and 'A follows reference alone does not assign old work.' Test-strategy duty 1 drops 'the spec changes since the run began (quoted below)' and says 'new or changed outcomes and the preservation set they affect' from RUN/current-spec.md, which duty 1 of spec initializes as the full prior aggregate.

experiment.description: Fixture a current-spec that is the prior aggregate plus one new acceptance line on R-1, with deferred R-9 still present. Give one planner arm the new plan duties and record its work_items. A second arm is the same packet with the quoted prior-vs-current diff included.
experiment.success: The first arm's work_items follow only R-1 (plus an evidenced prerequisite) and include no implementation item whose follows is R-9 or any other unchanged requirement.

findings.claim: Requirement text written during the run is stored in a run-local file that the commit and handoff rules do not keep, while durable skills are told to link there. Implement, document, carry-forward, and step review add spec lines to RUN/current-spec.md. The step commit set is still the item paths, docs, and KNOWLEDGE/. Step review is also told to edit only inside the item paths and KNOWLEDGE/. Carry-forward tells new skills to link to RUN/current-spec.md. Handoff then checks KNOWLEDGE/spec.md from the returned project without the run directory, and can restore or replace the candidate from RUN/spec/reviewed.md after those lines were added.
findings.evidence: Implement duty 4, document duty 3, and carry-forward duty 1 move R-<n> writes from KNOWLEDGE/spec.md to RUN/current-spec.md. Carry-forward 3.4 changes skill links from KNOWLEDGE/spec.md to RUN/current-spec.md. Step-plan duty 7 still says the item commit takes the item paths, changed documentation, and KNOWLEDGE/. The review focus says fix within the item paths and KNOWLEDGE, then separately to add evidence in RUN/current-spec.md. Handoff duty 5 seals reviewed.md and says not to edit the candidate; duty 7 still repairs KNOWLEDGE/spec.md and says the check is done without the run directory.

experiment.description: On a fixture run, have document append a step-marked line to R-1 in RUN/current-spec.md and have carry-forward create a skill whose only requirement link is RUN/current-spec.md#R-1. Accept the step commit with the published path set, delete the RUN directory, then perform the handoff promotion and the durable-link check.
experiment.success: The step commit or the promoted KNOWLEDGE/spec.md contains that step-marked line, and the committed skill link resolves to that requirement from the returned repository after RUN/ is gone.

findings.claim: A requested replacement of one clause has no single legal outcome. The spec duty says to preserve history and replace only conflicting clauses, and also says to fix any required requirement that was dropped or weakened versus the prior. Conflicting is undefined, and the ## Retired destination was removed. The stage can refuse the replacement, delete the old clause with no retained reason, or leave the old and new clauses both in force. Duty 5 still says 'Title spec.md', so the same stage can also retitle the aggregate file it is told not to edit until handoff.
findings.evidence: Spec duty 1 after text: 'Preserve IDs, history and deferred clauses; current explicit instructions replace only their conflicting clauses.' The before text required a ## Retired move and said current instructions supersede older clauses. Duty 10 still requires fixing 'a required requirement, test ID or case dropped or weakened compared with the prior accepted version.' Duty 5 still says 'Title spec.md for the product, not for one request' while the edited file is RUN/current-spec.md and KNOWLEDGE/spec.md is supposed to stay the prior aggregate.

experiment.description: Prior R-1 has acceptance lines A and B. User text: 'Replace A with A2 and keep B.' Run three spec-stage trials from the same packet. Compare the candidate to the prior snapshot.
experiment.success: Every trial contains A2, keeps B's text, and records A once as retired with the user instruction as the reason, with no second active A and no edit to KNOWLEDGE/spec.md before promotion.

findings.claim: Discovery, research, and plan can spend the shared exploration allowance on unbounded Git history and record superseded or volatile commit text as knowledge. They require full messages past the recent-three or recent window, including empty learning commits, and retention of the decision, alternatives, rationale, and exact revision. In discovery that retention sits on the KNOWLEDGE/environment.md write, whose entries are marked binding, observed practice, or proposal. No duty gives a stop count, prefers the current AD over an older commit, or keeps version and command text out of that durable file.
findings.evidence: Discovery duty 3 adds: 'read the relevant full Git messages even beyond the recent-three window, including empty learning commits; retain the decision, alternatives, rationale and exact revision' immediately before 'Record in KNOWLEDGE/environment.md' with each item 'marked binding requirement, observed practice or proposal.' Research duty 2 and plan duty 1 repeat the beyond-the-window retrieval. Discovery duty 8 still gives one shared exploration allowance. Plan duty 10 still says to copy no transcript. The evidence statement says not to require all-history rereads, but the new duties require reading past the window.

experiment.description: Repository with a current AD-4, an older empty learning commit whose message records a rejected alternative and a pinned old runtime version, and 30 unrelated commits outside the recent-three window. Run discovery and inspect KNOWLEDGE/environment.md and the discovery allowance outcome.
experiment.success: The environment record cites the relevant current revision as a locator, does not mark the rejected alternative or the old version pin as a binding current fact, and discovery does not stop for allowance exhaustion because of those unrelated commits.

findings.claim: The batch does not show that intent is preserved. It is described as preliminary and not a final pass; knowledge, CRLF, and /var versus /private/var failures were closed by correcting assertions and fixtures; packet overruns were closed by shortening prompt text while leaving limits unchanged. The spec stage goal still says this run's ID changes come from the spec diff, while KNOWLEDGE/spec.md is defined to stay unchanged until promotion, so an aggregate diff stays empty for the whole run. No reported case checks an untouched subclause after promotion.
findings.evidence: The evidence text says the hermetic results 'are not final passes,' cites 26 corrected locator assertions, 3 CRLF fixture assertions, 3 path-injection failures from /var versus /private/var, and 13 overruns fixed by shortening text. goal_diff sets the spec goal to RUN/current-spec.md but retains 'ShipLoop derives this run's ID changes from the spec diff.' Spec duty 1 says KNOWLEDGE/spec.md remains the prior aggregate until final handoff. The same evidence says the independent review fixes are not all verified and that no accuracy evaluation has been run.

experiment.description: On a dirty-start checkout, change only RUN/current-spec.md, then compute the run's added, changed, and retired IDs with the documented spec diff of KNOWLEDGE/spec.md and again with a diff against the bound RUN/spec/prior-spec.md bytes. Repeat promotion once via the /var path and once via the /private/var real path, including a CRLF prior file.
experiment.success: Both ID derivations return the same non-empty delta, and both promotions write one byte-identical KNOWLEDGE/spec.md that matches the reviewed candidate with newlines unchanged.
